payload.analysis: Combined with the suspected secondary restless legs syndrome, retrieved results show severe iron deficiency (ferritin 2.0 ng/mL, iron 2.0 μmol/L) and anemia (Hb 63 g/L), which strongly support iron-deficiency-driven RLS. The therapeutic olanzapine level (53.5 ng/mL) with reported dose-related worsening further implicates medication contribution. Normal physical exam excludes focal neurological causes, and the characteristic nocturnal symptoms with movement relief fit secondary RLS. All key information for confirming this hypothesis is covered.

payload.report: Characteristic nocturnal limb discomfort relieved by movement, severe iron deficiency (ferritin 2.0 ng/mL, iron 2.0 μmol/L), and anemia (Hb 63 g/L) strongly support secondary restless legs syndrome (RLS). Normal exam and therapeutic olanzapine level with dose-related worsening indicate medication contributes rather than primarily causes it. This refutes drug-induced movement disorder and psychiatric sleep disturbance. Final: iron-deficiency-driven secondary RLS, olanzapine contributing.
